# Data and hot-path audit - 2026-10-18

Scope: standalone Stage A geometry/editor/viewers and the read-only
[Festapp data boundary](FESTAPP-DATA-BOUNDARY.md). No production data, database,
reservations, pricing owner or Festapp runtime was changed. Initial findings were
read-only; the coordinator then authorized the narrow fixes and hot-path work
recorded below.

## Reservation and identity findings

The model enforces UUID identity/reference namespaces, valid parent kinds,
acyclic bounded-depth hierarchy, unique seat membership, valid attachments,
immutable snapshots and closed visual properties. Clone/preset operations remap
explicit references without treating displayed text as an identifier.

Three concrete bypasses were fixed:

1. An omitted/null v1 selection-unit kind behaved atomically in pickers but did
   not enter the controller's atomic reservation guard. The immutable model now
   normalizes both legacy spellings to `kind: atomic`; explicit unknown kinds
   still reject. Input payloads are not mutated. The generated schema explicitly
   accepts omitted/null/atomic spellings. See
   [model.dart](../../packages/venue_layout_core/lib/src/model.dart:262) and
   [selection-unit compatibility tests](../../packages/venue_layout_core/test/selection_unit_compatibility_test.dart).
2. A protected standalone seat could be replaced with another node kind keeping
   its UUID. The controller now requires protected identities to remain actual
   seat nodes, rather than accepting any matching node ID.
3. The guard previously checked only old units. A protected standalone seat
   could acquire a new paired unit, or join a previously free unit. Protection
   now checks membership in both directions, including undo/redo. See
   [controller protection](../../lib/src/layout_editor/venue_layout_controller.dart:224)
   and [reservation regressions](../../test/layout/reservation_identity_test.dart).

Table shrink retains protected seat IDs and removes only eligible free seats;
if protected members cannot fit it rejects atomically. Couch count changes
preserve cushion/unit IDs for retained slots; any protected couch member freezes
atomic membership in both directions. Locked geometry remains independently
protected. Host reservation state is supplied through `protectedSeatIds` and
`constraints`; it is never persisted in appearance or geometry.

The Flutter picker lifecycle/status findings were handed to the coordinator:
it now resets document-session state and fences old asynchronous results by a
generation, and checks blocked/sold alongside other unavailable statuses. That
change is owned and verified by the coordinator, not by this audit worker.

## Explicit membership and production boundary

Membership is queryable from the model without label heuristics:

- `node.kind == seat` identifies a seat. `parentId` resolves its immediate
  spatial owner. Canonical table seats have a table parent; couch cushions have
  a furniture parent with `furniture: couch`. Other/group/no-parent cases are
  distinct; no implicit pricing relationship is inferred.
- `selectionUnits[].nodeIds` is the separate atomic customer-selection
  relationship. `attachments` describes table placement/anchors and must agree
  with the seat's parent. Neither is a spot/product/order binding.
- `couchSeatCount` reads materialized direct child seats. Helper-generated
  couches own one atomic unit. Generic validated documents can still describe
  a couch without all children in one unit; the validator does not impose a
  complete couch-specific topology. This remains an authoring/import policy
  consideration, not an automatic reservation mapping.

A protected seat may still be detached or reattached to another table while
retaining its ID and protected unit membership, unless the host `constraints`
callback rejects it. `attachSeat` accepts only a table target; a generic document
edit can assign a furniture parent. The package guard protects identity and
atomic membership, not a commercial product/price/spot binding. Production must
check such transfers in its authoritative transaction. A parent change must
never be treated as permission to rewrite an already sold price.

Stage B remains necessary: explicit node UUID to existing DB spot-ID bindings,
strict live availability loading, group product-default migration, individual
price exceptions, server-side reservation/expiry/locking and save-revision
conflicts are not integrated in Stage A. Current Festapp groups serialize only
`id/title`; object `group` is the persisted membership authority and the DB spot
owns product/order/hold state. The standalone example uses synthetic prices and
selection callbacks, not production reservations. In particular, a missing host
presentation is not evidence that a production seat is available.

## Appearance contract

Appearance is an optional sparse document map, resolved by node kind; explicit
`appearanceOverrides` opt properties back into local ownership. The strict
whitelist includes fill, stroke, strokeWidth, cornerRadius, opacity, color and
seatStyle (`plain/wood/upholstered`). Fonts remain in `defaultTextStyle`.
Global edits preserve node IDs, parents, attachments, atomic units and geometry.
Open lines remain unfilled. Presentation status colors take precedence.
Wood/upholstered details are decoration belonging to the same node and do not
create hit targets or selectable entities. Sofa cushions retain sofa rendering.
The common core scene feeds both renderers and partial scene compilation.

## Bounded performance evidence

Diagnostic environment: Apple M5, arm64, macOS 27.0.1, Dart 3.13.2 stable. These
are warmed Dart VM microbenchmarks on a shared workstation, not Flutter frame,
browser, AOT, phone or release-budget claims. Each case discards one warm-up and
reports the median of five samples. Corpus: straight rows, 100 seats per row,
500/5000 seats, no rendered seat labels or external resources. Wood adds one
scene decoration per seat. Initial full-scene measurements used a new immutable
snapshot after transform/validation; this is not application cold-start timing.

| Seats/style | Transform + validate ms | Full scene ms | Four effective-property reads per seat ms | Six-kind preset validations ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 500/plain | 2.662 | 2.825 | 1.778 | 14.256 |
| 500/wood | 2.482 | 3.460 | 1.736 | 14.580 |
| 5000/plain | 26.110 | 35.013 | 18.602 | 156.975 |
| 5000/wood | 26.191 | 47.139 | 20.745 | 154.346 |

The property-read probe reproduces the original repeated resolver pattern; it
does not time actual inspector widgets. The coordinator's inspector refactor
moves full-plan color collection to color-picker opening and retains layer rows
across geometry-only changes. Six sequential `setLayoutAppearance` calls still
validate six full snapshots; batch-setting appearance once is a future isolated
optimization if larger-plan style editing needs it.

The audit replaced controller whole-document JSON no-op/dirty checks and
per-node JSON diffs with shared immutable structural comparisons. It also made
selection reads O(1) immutable snapshots, and indexed furniture unit capacities
once per scene context instead of repeatedly scanning member/node lists.

| Seats | Old canonical JSON document compare ms | Shared document compare ms | Old per-node JSON diff ms | Shared node diff ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 500 | 2.525 | 0.001 | 1.725 | 0.011 |
| 5000 | 29.900 | 0.009 | 16.496 | 0.046 |

The document comparison case moves the first/root node, allowing an early exit;
these timings are not a claim that every comparison is constant-time. Node diff
visits all nodes, reusing immutable identity for unchanged nodes. Reordered
records preserve canonical equality through a rare serialization fallback.

The coordinator separately measured the new incremental scene cache at 5000
static seats plus a moving six-chair table: full scene 23.536 ms versus cached
partial update 2.216 ms median over eight samples, with exact canonical scene
equality. See [scene-cache benchmark](../../tool/benchmark_layout_scene_cache.dart).
That probe prevalidates snapshots and therefore does not include the remaining
validation cost.

Full validation still walks a changed snapshot and serializes its canonical
payload for the 8 MiB budget; see
[model payload check](../../packages/venue_layout_core/lib/src/model.dart:627).
Canvas/lock checks and subtree/matrix work also remain proportional to document
size. Consequently these improvements do not establish a 16.7 ms end-to-end
5000-seat drag budget. Measure the integrated editor before attempting a safely
bounded incremental validator; do not weaken import validation or trust a caller
supplied changed-ID list as a validation bypass.
